'''Tie:''' {{legend0|#d2b1d9|40–50%}} {{legend0|#ae8bb1|50%}} | title = [[Governor of Massachusetts|Governor]] | before_election = [[Charlie Baker]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Charlie Baker]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsMA}} The '''2018 Massachusetts gubernatorial election''' took place on November 6, 2018, to elect the [[Governor of Massachusetts|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Massachusetts|lieutenant governor]] of the [[Massachusetts|Commonwealth of Massachusetts]]. [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] Governor [[Charlie Baker]] and Lieutenant Governor [[Karyn Polito]] won election to a second term in office, defeating [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] challengers [[Jay Gonzalez (politician)|Jay Gonzalez]] and [[Quentin Palfrey]], respectively. Candidates were selected in the [[Partisan primary|primary election]] held on September 4, 2018. This was one of eight Republican-held governorships up for election in a state that [[Hillary Clinton]] won in the [[2016 United States presidential election in Massachusetts|2016 presidential election]]. Despite Massachusetts's Democratic lean at the presidential level, Charlie Baker retained high approval ratings and was expected to safely win re-election. Shortly after polls closed at 8 p.m. local time, the [[Associated Press]] declared the race in favor of incumbents Baker and Polito.{{cite news |url=https://www.boston.com/news/politics/2018/11/06/massachusetts-election-results-2018/ |title=Here's an updating list of the 2018 Massachusetts election winners |first=Christopher |last=Gavin |website=[[Boston.com]] |date=November 6, 2018 |access-date=November 6, 2018}} Shortly after 9 p.m. location time, Gonzalez conceded the election.{{cite tweet |user=MattPStout |number=1059993577026211840 |title=@jay4ma has conceded to @CharlieBakerMA |date=November 6, 2018 |access-date=November 6, 2018}} Baker was re-elected with the highest vote total in the history of Massachusetts gubernatorial elections and by the widest margin since [[Bill Weld]] was re-elected governor in [[1994 Massachusetts gubernatorial election|1994]]. He won many of the Commonwealth's most populated cities, including [[Worcester, Massachusetts|Worcester]], [[New Bedford]], and [[Springfield, Massachusetts|Springfield]].{{cite news |url=https://whdh.com/news/bakers-big-win-a-gop-anomaly-in-heavily-democratic-state/ |work=[[WHDH-TV]] |title=Baker's big win a GOP anomaly in heavily-Democratic state |date=November 7, 2018 |access-date=December 30, 2020}} Baker almost won [[Boston]], losing it by only around 3,000 votes, an extraordinary showing for a statewide Republican candidate in a major city. Baker also carried every county in the state.{{cite news |url=https://www.masslive.com/news/boston/2018/11/2018_massachusetts_election_re.html |work=MassLive |title=2018 Massachusetts Election: Republican Gov. Charlie Baker almost won Democrat-dominated Boston |date=November 7, 2018 |access-date=December 30, 2020}} {{As of|2026}}, this is the most recent election in which a Republican was elected to a statewide office in Massachusetts. {{TOC limit|3}} ==Background== Charlie Baker was elected in 2014 by a slim margin over then-Attorney General [[Martha Coakley]]; however, he was consistently rated as one of the most popular governors in the country.{{cite web|url=https://boston.cbslocal.com/2018/04/12/charlie-baker-poll-morning-consult-most-popular/|title=Poll: Charlie Baker Is Once Again America's Most Popular Governor|date=April 12, 2018 |publisher=WBZ}} Some Democrats, including Congressman [[Michael Capuano|Mike Capuano]] and Speaker of the House [[Robert DeLeo (politician)|Bob DeLeo]] publicly, speculated that they might vote for Baker over the eventual Democratic nominee.{{cite web|url=http://www.bostonherald.com/news/us_politics/2017/08/mike_capuano_may_dodge_party_lines_in_gubernatorial_vote|title=Mike Capuano may dodge party lines in gubernatorial vote|date=23 August 2017 |publisher=Boston Herald}} Speculated candidates such as Attorney General [[Maura Healey]], Congressman [[Joe Kennedy III|Joe Kennedy]], former state senator [[Dan Wolf]], and [[Boston, Massachusetts|Boston]] Mayor [[Marty Walsh]] all declined to be candidates, leaving no prominent Democrats to challenge Baker, which was seen as a necessary prerequisite to mount a formidable challenge to him. Because Evan Falchuk received more than 3% of the vote in the [[Massachusetts gubernatorial election, 2014|2014 gubernatorial election]], the [[United Independent Party]] gained official status.{{cite news|url=http://news.wgbh.org/post/united-independent-party-gains-official-status|title=United Independent Party Gains Official Status|last=Emmanouilidou|first=Lydia|date=November 6, 2014|work=[[WGBH (FM)]]|access-date=7 November 2014|archive-date=September 20, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160920094359/http://news.wgbh.org/post/united-independent-party-gains-official-status|url-status=dead}} Falchuck had stated that he would "certainly" run for office in 2018.{{cite news|last=Morrison|first=Sara|title=The United Independent Party Is Official, and Evan Falchuk's Work Has Just Begun|newspaper=Boston.com|date=November 5, 2014|url=http://www.huffingtonpost.com/2014/11/17/future-democratic-candidates_n_6152346.html}} In 2016, however, the UIP lost its official party status after it failed to register 1% of Massachusetts voters as members.{{cite news|url=https://www.politico.com/states/massachusetts/story/2016/10/united-independent-party-loses-state-party-designation-106905|title=United Independent Party loses state party designation|last=Dezenski|first=Lauren|date=October 31, 2016|work=[[Politico]]|access-date=23 January 2017}} Falchuk later left the UIP and registered as a Democrat in early 2017.{{cite web|url=https://www.bostonglobe.com/metro/2017/02/12/switch/b84oZEjZyFyGSnn5OHl5jO/story.html#comments|title=Evan Falchuk, former gubernatorial candidate, switches from his independent party to Democratic - The Boston Globe|website=[[The Boston Globe]] |access-date=22 May 2018}}{{cite web|url=https://www.politico.com/states/massachusetts/story/2016/10/united-independent-party-loses-state-party-designation-106905|title=United Independent Party loses state party designation|website=[[Politico]] |date=October 31, 2016 |access-date=22 May 2018}} ==Republican primary== There was some concern amongst the Republican Party that Baker was too moderate, and there were talks of challenging him with a more conservative opponent in the primaries. GOP state committeeman Robert Cappucci told the ''[[Boston Herald]]'' that if Baker "shuns conservatives [...] there will be 100 percent an effort to try to find a conservative, viable candidate to challenge him in 2018 for governor". David Kopacz, the president of the Massachusetts Republican Assembly, also stated that Baker might face a conservative challenger in 2018.{{cite news|last1=Stout|first1=Matt|last2=Cassidy|first2=Chris|title=Waiting for Mr. Right: Conservative wing of GOP warns Charlie Baker|newspaper=Boston Herald|date=November 13, 2014}} Following his 2016 election, [[Barnstable County, Massachusetts|Barnstable County]] Commissioner Ron Beaty, who once was tried and convicted for threatening the life of President [[George H. W. Bush]],{{cite news|url=http://www.barnstablepatriot.com/home2/index.php/option=com_content/task=view/id=37289/Itemid=30|last=Hoffenburg|first=Noah|title=Ronald Beaty, Jr.|newspaper=Barnstable Patriot|date=August 29, 2014}} had been making local and state headlines. He proposed a "shark mitigation strategy" to combat the growing presence of sharks near [[Cape Cod]] beaches by baiting and shooting them, which was rejected for consideration by the commission chairman. He also mulled a primary run against his state representative, [[Randy Hunt (politician)|Randy Hunt]], after Hunt parked in his Barnstable County Courthouse parking spot. In September 2017 he announced he was in the process of changing the purpose of his campaign committee from a county to a statewide office. He cited the governor's criticisms of President [[Donald Trump]] and his willingness to work with Democrats as his inspiration to run. On December 8, 2017, Scott Lively announced his campaign.{{cite web | url=https://sites.google.com/view/thirdpartywatch/secret/scott-lively-former-independent-candidate-is-running-for-the-republican?authuser=2 | title=Scott Lively, Former Independent Candidate, Is Running For The Republican Nomination | publisher=Third Party Watch | date=December 8, 2017}} On December 13, 2017, Beaty stated he was no longer considering a run against Baker.{{cite web|url=http://www.capecodtoday.com/article/2017/12/13/236270-Beaty-Ends-Exploratory-Project-Gov-Run|title=Beaty Ends Exploratory Project on Gov. Run - CapeCodToday.com|website=www.capecodtoday.com|access-date=22 May 2018|archive-date=13 December 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171213203337/http://capecodtoday.com/article/2017/12/13/236270-Beaty-Ends-Exploratory-Project-Gov-Run|url-status=dead}} [[Scott Lively]], an evangelical pastor, challenged Baker and received more than the 15% of delegate votes necessary at the state convention to qualify for ballot access. Baker won the endorsement of the party by an overwhelming margin.{{cite web|url=https://worcestermag.com/2018/04/28/baker-earns-states-gop-endorsement-for-governor-scott-lively-forces-primary/59244|title=Baker earns states GOP endorsement for governor; Scott Lively forces primary - Worcester Mag|first=Walter Jr.|last=Bird|date=28 April 2018|access-date=22 May 2018}}{{Dead link|date=April 2023 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }} Baker ultimately won the nomination, but not without Lively securing 36 percent of the primary vote, leading to speculation that Baker's more moderate disposition and opposition to President Trump might have damaged his general election chances with Republican base voters.{{cite web | url=https://commonwealthmagazine.org/politics/the-bay-state-trump-bump-2/ | title=The Bay State Trump bump | publisher=Commonwealth Magazine | date=September 5, 2018 | access-date=September 5, 2018 | archive-date=September 5, 2018 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180905214927/https://commonwealthmagazine.org/politics/the-bay-state-trump-bump-2/ | url-status=dead }} ===Governor=== ====Candidates==== =====Declared===== * [[Charlie Baker]], incumbent governor{{cite news|url=https://www.boston.com/news/politics/2017/11/28/charlie-baker-confirms-run-for-2nd-term-as-massachusetts-governor/|title=Charlie Baker confirms run for 2nd term as Massachusetts governor|work=[[The Boston Globe]]|last=Salsberg|first=Bob|date=November 28, 2017|access-date=November 28, 2017}} * [[Scott Lively]], pastor and independent candidate for governor in [[Massachusetts gubernatorial election, 2014|2014]]{{cite news|url=http://www.masslive.com/politics/index.ssf/2017/12/anti-lgbt_springfield_pastor_s.html|title=Anti-LGBT Springfield pastor Scott Lively to challenge Gov.
